aspects.says: Injecting a Clock instead of calling now() makes time-dependent code testable.
aspects.reason: practised on 7.3.2.2 (audit-log) and 7.3.2.1 (age), where a fixed Clock drives the code

aspects.says: ZonedDateTime moves a time in a DST gap forward, and plusHours differs from plusDays across a DST change.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: DST arithmetic is the subject of 7.3.2.5 (zoned and offset date and time), whose page practises it

aspects.says: Duration is a time-based amount (hours, minutes, seconds) and Period a date-based one (years, months, days).
ZonedDateTime.equals compares the zone too, while isEqual compares only the instant.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: a ZonedDateTime comparison rule, the subject of 7.3.2.5 (zoned and offset date and time)

aspects.says: A fluent call such as with(TemporalAdjusters.next(MONDAY)) only has an effect when its returned value is kept.
Every java.time object is immutable: plus and with return a new object and leave the original unchanged.
java.time prints ISO-8601 from toString() and parses it by default, so each type has its own recognisable text form.
Instant does not model leap seconds; it uses a smoothed timeline.
aspects.reason: incidental detail that no test can observe

aspects.says: plusMonths clamps the day to the end of a shorter month, so January 31 plus one month is February 29 in 2024.
aspects.reason: practised on 7.3.2.1, whose billing practice checks end-of-month clamping

aspects.says: The temporal interfaces are not sealed, so a pattern switch over the concrete java.time types needs a default branch.
java.time is null-hostile, throwing NullPointerException for a null argument, and a value class built on it refuses null the same way.
Local, offset and zoned date-times and instants are different types, chosen by whether a value carries no zone, an offset, a region zone or is a UTC point.
Instant fits timestamps, LocalDate birthdays and holidays, LocalTime opening hours and ZonedDateTime cross-zone scheduling.
Months are 1-based and invalid values throw DateTimeException immediately.
aspects.reason: practised on 7.3.1, whose legacy-fields and strict-parse practices check 1-based months and fail-fast validation

aspects.says: java.time.format, java.time.temporal, java.time.zone and java.time.chrono hold formatting, fields and adjusters, zone rules and other calendars.
